confidence_note: Book is Atomic Habits (2018); DB metadata off. Two-Minute Rule examples (read one page, take out the yoga mat, put on running shoes) appear in summaries and are close to the book's list; exact wording not verified so they are paraphrased. Old TR meditation-app example not used. The book says the goal is mastering showing up, not staying at two minutes.
facts: Clear's Two-Minute Rule: when you start a new habit it should take less than two minutes to do.
Examples: 'read before bed' becomes 'read one page'; 'run' becomes 'put on running shoes'; 'do yoga' becomes 'take out the yoga mat'.
Starting is the hard part; once you have started, continuing is easier.
The two minutes is a gateway: the point is to master the habit of showing up, not to stay at two minutes forever.
A habit must be established before it can be improved.
tension: The evening arrives, the sofa wins, and the workout never starts.
opening_idea: Open on the shoes by the door at the end of a long day.

lessons.idea: Shrink the first step until it is easy to say yes, then let the habit grow.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A person who avoids paperwork opens the folder only.

reflect_final: Which habit do you keep postponing, and what is the smallest first step you could do in under two minutes tonight?

use_cases.situation: A teammate avoids a long task.
use_cases.move: Suggest opening the document and writing one line.
Tell a friend you will only put on your shoes.

use_cases.situation: Your child will not start homework.

pocket_idea: If the habit feels heavy, shrink it to putting on the shoes or reading one page, and let the rest follow.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Clear's habit trick is to make the first step so small it is silly: put on the shoes, read one page.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: The Two-Minute Rule shrinks a habit to a two-minute start, such as one page or tying shoes, because starting is the hardest part.
